Admin.description: The admin HTTP server: health, metrics and the management API.

listen.description:
Addresses to listen on, as `ip:port`. A non-loopback address needs
`token`.

token.description: Bearer token for the admin API.

Balance.description:
How a push consumer picks the endpoint for each attempt, among those
whose circuit breaker admits a request.

oneOf.description: Sticky by chat (or user); round robin without either.
The endpoint with the fewest requests in flight.

allow_local_files.description:
Let `file:` references (files on the server's own disk) reach an
upstream in local mode. Off, the gateway and webhook replies refuse
them, so a client cannot read the server's files through tgin.

api_url.description:
Bot API base URL: shorthand for an unnamed `cloud` upstream, which
`/v1/config` and metrics call `api_url`. Not with `upstream`.
Supports `${env:…}` and `${file:…}`.

gateway.description:
The Bot API gateway for this bot's downstream clients. Changes apply
live.

ingress.description: How updates arrive; at most one. Omitted, the bot receives none.

name.description: Unique bot name, used in metrics and logs.

routes.description: Rules in order; the first match wins.

token.description:
The bot token: only ASCII letters, digits, `:`, `_` and `-`. The Bot
API gateway serves only tokens shaped `<digits>:<secret>`.

upstream.description: The `upstreams` entry this bot talks to. Not with `api_url`.

failure_threshold.description:
Consecutive transient failures (408, 429, 5xx, timeouts, network
errors) that open the breaker; at least 1.

open_for.description: How long the breaker stays open; above 0.

ByteSize.description: A size of at least 1 MiB: bytes, or a number with `B`, `KiB`, `MiB` or `GiB`.

burst.description:
Requests let through at once before the rate applies; at
least 1.

per.description: The period `count` requests are spread over; above 0.

Cidr.description: An IP network such as `10.0.0.0/8`, or a single address.

oneOf.description: Bots fetch updates from tgin with `getUpdates`.
tgin posts updates to HTTP endpoints.

Duration.description: A duration such as `500ms`, `1.5s`, `5m` or `1h 30m`, or `0`. Month (`M`) and year (`y`) units are rejected.

Files.description:
Where a local server's files are: `dir` (with `server_dir`) or `url`.
The server keeps each bot's files in a directory named after its token
(`:` replaced by `~` where its filesystem refuses `:`); tgin serves a
bot only its own.

dir.description:
The server's files directory (its `--files-dir`, or `--dir` when
that is unset) as mounted in tgin; read-only is enough. A relative
path is relative to the config file's directory. Supports `${env:…}`
and `${file:…}`.

server_dir.description:
The same directory as the server sees it, an absolute path; only
with `dir`, which it defaults to. Supports `${env:…}` and
`${file:…}`.

url.description:
An HTTP origin serving the server's files directory (its
`--files-dir`, or `--dir` when that is unset), `http` or `https`.
Supports `${env:…}` and `${file:…}`.

Gateway.description:
The Bot API gateway: how tgin forwards the bot's requests from
downstream clients to the Bot API.

upstream_idle_timeout.description:
Longest wait for the Bot API to accept or send the next bytes of a
request; at least 1s. A transfer that keeps moving is never cut.

GlobalRate.description: Requests of the bot, over all chats.

burst.description:
Requests let through at once before the rate applies; at
least 1.

per.description: The period `count` requests are spread over; above 0.

GroupRate.description:
Requests per group, supergroup or channel (a negative `chat_id` or an
`@username`), on top of `per_chat`.

burst.description:
Requests let through at once before the rate applies; at
least 1.

per.description: The period `count` requests are spread over; above 0.

oneOf.description: Receive updates on the data-plane server.

format.description: Log line format; a change takes effect after a restart.

level.description:
The most verbose level logged; a reload applies it. A non-empty
`RUST_LOG` overrides it.

LongPoll.description: Long polling: tgin calls `getUpdates` on the Bot API.

allowed_updates.description:
Update types to receive, sent with every `getUpdates`, so the config
decides what arrives. Omitted, tgin sends `[]`: Telegram's default,
every type except `chat_member`, `message_reaction` and
`message_reaction_count`.

delete_webhook_on_start.description:
Call `deleteWebhook` (keeping pending updates) before polling, and
again when a poll finds a webhook set. Off, an active webhook stops
the polling until something else deletes it.

Match.description:
Rule predicates: values within a list are alternatives, fields must all
hold, and an empty list matches anything.

commands.description:
Commands, with or without the leading `/`: 1 to 32 ASCII letters,
digits or `_`, with no `@bot` suffix.

OnFull.description: What a full queue does with a new update.

oneOf.description: Refuse it; the source retries later.

Ordering.description: The order a consumer hands out updates in.

oneOf.description: Queue order, any number per chat at once.

One update per chat (or user) in flight at a time; updates with
neither are never held back.

Pull.description:
Bots fetch updates from tgin with `getUpdates` on
`/c/<consumer>/getUpdates` and on each alias.

aliases.description:
Extra HTTP paths serving this consumer, matched as written, with the
same rules as a webhook `path`. Each supports `${env:…}` and
`${file:…}`.

honor_drop_pending.description:
Let `deleteWebhook` with `drop_pending_updates: true`, sent on this
consumer's gateway path, drop the calling bot's queued updates;
those another bot left before a reload stay. Off, the flag is
ignored.

lease_timeout.description:
How long a fetched update waits for its acknowledgement before
another poll may receive it; at least 1s.

Push.description:
tgin posts each update to HTTP endpoints, with retries and a circuit
breaker per endpoint.

accept_set_webhook.description:
Let `setWebhook`, sent on this consumer's gateway path, add its URL
as an endpoint until tgin restarts, instead of answering it without
effect. Only for a consumer fed by one bot. Whoever holds that bot's
token then chooses where tgin posts its updates, from inside your
network: enable it only for trusted downstreams.

endpoints.description:
Where updates are posted. Empty only with `accept_set_webhook: true`;
updates then queue until a `setWebhook` gives an endpoint.

honor_drop_pending.description:
Let `deleteWebhook`, or a `setWebhook` this consumer accepts, with
`drop_pending_updates: true`, sent on this consumer's gateway path,
drop the calling bot's queued updates; other bots' stay. Off, the
flag is ignored.

max_in_flight.description:
Most deliveries at once over all endpoints, counting those waiting
to retry.

RateLimit.description: Telegram's flood limits, applied before a request goes upstream.

max_delay.description:
Longest delay `shape` adds before it answers 429 instead; at most
1m. `0s` behaves like `reject`.

methods.description:
The methods limited, ignoring case: a method name, or a prefix
followed by `*`. At least one unless `mode: off`.

RateMode.description: What a request beyond the limits gets.

oneOf.description:
Delayed until the limits admit it, up to `max_delay`; a longer wait
is answered with 429 at once.

Reload.description: Hot reload of the config file.

debounce.description: Quiet time after a change before reloading; at least 10ms.

drain_timeout.description: How long a removed consumer drains before it is dropped.

watch.description: Reload when the config file changes.

max_age.description:
Age after which the update is dead-lettered, counted from when it
was queued; above 0.

max_attempts.description: Attempts before the update is dead-lettered; at least 1.

Retry429.description: The transparent retry of a request the Bot API answered with 429.

max_wait.description:
Longest `retry_after` waited out before the one retry; at most 1m.
A longer one passes the 429 through; `0s` turns the retry off.

match.description: When the rule applies. Omitted, it matches every update.

to.description: Where matching updates go; every entry receives the update.

Runtime.description:
Process settings. `worker_threads` takes effect after a restart; a
shutdown uses the `lame_duck` and `shutdown_grace` of the config in
effect when it begins.

lame_duck.description:
How long, once shutdown begins, tgin keeps serving while readiness
reports "not ready", before it stops ingesting; skipped without a
`server` block.

shutdown_grace.description: How long shutdown waits for queues to drain.

worker_threads.description: Tokio worker threads: `auto` (one per CPU) or a count.

Secret.description: A secret. Supports `${env:NAME}` and `${file:PATH}` (relative to the config file); `$${` is a literal `${`.

header_read_timeout.description: How long a client may take to send the request headers; above 0.

tls.description:
Serve HTTPS with these files. Turning TLS on or off takes effect
after a restart.

trusted_proxies.description: Proxies whose `X-Forwarded-For` is trusted, as networks.

Split.description: Exactly one child of `among` receives each update.

among.description: The children: consumer names or nested targets.

weights.description: One weight per `among` entry, each above 0; only with `weighted`.

SplitStrategy.description: How a split picks its child.

oneOf.description: Sticky by chat (or user); round robin without either.

Target.description: A consumer name, `{split: …}` (one child receives the update) or `{all: […]}` (every child does).

TextMatch.description: A text match; each list is non-empty.

oneOf.description: Any of these regexes matches somewhere in the text.

Tls.description:
The data plane's certificate. Every config reload reads both files
again and swaps the certificate in if they changed.

cert_file.description:
PEM certificate chain file; a relative path is relative to the config
file's directory. Supports `${env:…}` and `${file:…}`.

key_file.description:
PEM private key file; a relative path is relative to the config
file's directory. Supports `${env:…}` and `${file:…}`.

Upstream.description:
A Bot API server: Telegram's (`cloud`) or a self-hosted
`telegram-bot-api` (`local`).

files.description:
How tgin serves the bots' files on `/file/bot<token>/…`. Only with
`kind: local`; omitted, it serves none.

kind.description: `cloud` or `local`: which webhook, file and timeout rules apply.

local_mode.description:
The server runs with `--local`: it accepts `file:` uploads from its
own disk, answers `getFile` with absolute paths, and posts webhooks
over `http` to any port. Only with `kind: local`.

url.description:
The server's base URL, `http` or `https`; plain `http` to a host
that is not loopback warns. Supports `${env:…}` and `${file:…}`.

oneOf.description: Telegram's Bot API, or a server with its rules.

Webhook.description: Telegram posts updates to the data plane.

allowed_updates.description:
Update types to receive, sent with `setWebhook`, so the config decides
what arrives. Omitted, tgin sends `[]`: Telegram's default, every type
except `chat_member`, `message_reaction` and `message_reaction_count`.

certificate_file.description:
Self-signed certificate to upload with `setWebhook`; needs
`register: true`. A relative path is relative to the config file's
directory. Supports `${env:…}` and `${file:…}`.

ip_allowlist.description:
Who may post updates: `none` (anyone), `telegram` (Telegram's
published networks; not for a `local` upstream) or a list of
networks.

max_connections.description:
Telegram's `max_connections`: 1 to 100, or to 100000 for an
upstream in local mode.

path.description:
HTTP path updates are posted to. Omitted, `/webhook/<bot name>`. It
is matched as written, so it must be what a URL sends: no `?`, `#`,
spaces, control or non-ASCII characters, `.`/`..` segments or `\`.
Supports `${env:…}` and `${file:…}`.

public_url.description:
The public base URL the Bot API server reaches tgin at; `setWebhook`
registers it followed by `path`. `https` on port 443, 80, 88 or
8443, except for an upstream in local mode, which takes `http` and
any port. Supports `${env:…}` and `${file:…}`.

secret_token.description:
`auto` (derived from the bot token), `none`, or the secret Telegram
must send: 1 to 256 ASCII letters, digits, `_` or `-`.

WebhookReply.description:
What tgin does with a Bot API method call in an endpoint's response
body, the way Telegram handles a webhook reply.

oneOf.description:
Call the method through the gateway, once, before the update is
acknowledged.

anyOf.description: Derived from the bot token (HMAC-SHA256); the same on every restart and replica.

description:
The configuration file, version 1.

Only secrets (`token`, `secret_token`, `auth_token`, `admin.token`) and
fields holding URLs or file paths expand `${env:NAME}` and `${file:PATH}`
references; every other value is literal.

bots.description: The Telegram bots updates come from.

server.description:
The data plane: webhook ingress and pull consumers. Omitted, tgin
serves neither.

upstreams.description:
Bot API servers, by name, that bots reference with `upstream`. A
bot with `api_url`, or with neither field, talks to an unnamed
`cloud` upstream instead.

version.description: The config format version; must be 1.
